title: Document Search & Pattern Matching
short_description: Learn how document-management systems search words, locate patterns, provide prefix-based suggestions and analyze common text efficiently.

real_world_context.problem: A document-management system may contain thousands or millions of words across many documents. Users need to search for words, locate repeated patterns, receive relevant auto-complete suggestions, count words beginning with a prefix, and identify common text shared by document names.
real_world_context.why_it_matters: Efficient text searching and indexing allow document systems to respond quickly even when the amount of stored text becomes very large.

learning_objectives: Understand how document text can be represented using strings and arrays of words.
Understand the difference between linear search and efficient pattern matching.
Understand how KMP avoids unnecessary character comparisons.
Understand how a Trie supports prefix-based searching and auto-complete.
Apply prefix counting to indexed document words.
Find the longest common prefix shared by multiple document names.
Understand how algorithm choice affects performance as text data size increases.
completion_message: You have completed the Document Search & Pattern Matching mission. You have learned how searching, pattern matching, Trie-based indexing and prefix techniques can be applied to common document-management problems.
